simple.inThisVerse: The selected word is tied to מֶשִׁי (H4897) in the Hebrew source text. Part of speech: n-m.
simple.whyItMatters: This word appears 2 times in the Hebrew Bible, so BibleIQ can compare how Scripture uses it across multiple passages.
simple.summary: מֶשִׁי (meshîy) means silk (as drawn from the cocoon) First listed occurrence: Ezek 16 10.

definitions.full: H4897. meshi מֶ֫שִׁי noun [masculine] a costly material for garments, according to Rabb silk , (so Now Archaeology i. 124 ); whether this is based on actual tradition is dubious (etymology unknown); — absolute ׳מ Ezek 16:13 (|| שֵׁשׁ ), מֶ֑שִׁי 16:10 (|| id. ) See, further Thes Sm Da Berthol. ᵐ5 τρίχαπτα . מֻשִׁי see מוּשִׁי .
